headline: A 2018 law requires the Interior Department to provide burial containers for veterans buried in certain National Park Service cemeteries, with limits on what families may have to pay.
what_it_does: The law requires the Department of the Interior to provide outer burial receptacles, such as grave liners or burial vaults, for veterans buried in national cemeteries run by the National Park Service. An outer burial receptacle is a container that protects the casket and keeps the grave from sinking. For receptacles other than grave liners, Interior may pay back the cost, but it may require survivors to cover the amount above a grave liner's cost and related administrative costs.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans buried in National Park Service national cemeteries
who_it_affects.how: Their remains are to receive an outer burial receptacle provided by Interior.

who_it_affects.group: Families and survivors of veterans buried in these cemeteries
who_it_affects.how: They may be asked to pay the extra cost of a non-grave-liner receptacle above a grave liner's price, plus related administrative costs, if Interior seeks reimbursement.

who_it_affects.group: Department of the Interior and National Park Service
who_it_affects.how: They must provide outer burial receptacles for these veterans and manage any reimbursement from survivors.
